Your project was initialized with **PowerShell** (`"script": "ps"`), which is recorded here:

- `.specify/init-options.json` → `"script": "ps"`
- `.specify/integration.json` → `integration_settings.cursor-agent.script`: `"ps"`

Speckit only installs scripts for that choice, so you have `.specify/scripts/powershell/` and the Cursor skills point at `.ps1` files. Without `pwsh`, those steps fail.

## Script options

At init (and when upgrading), Speckit supports:

| Value | Runtime | Typical on macOS |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| `sh` | Bash shell scripts | Default — no extra install |
| `py` | Python scripts | Needs `python3` |
| `ps` | PowerShell | Needs `pwsh` |

## Switch an existing project (recommended on Mac)

From the repo root:

```bash
cd /Users/ankitsinghal/cursor-ai/ticket_management_app
specify integration upgrade cursor-agent --script sh --force
```

That should:

1. Write `.specify/scripts/bash/` (and refresh shared Spec Kit files)
2. Set `"script": "sh"` in `init-options.json` and `integration.json`
3. Refresh `.cursor/skills/speckit-*` so they call `.sh` instead of `.ps1`

`--force` overwrites managed Spec Kit files when switching runtimes; your integration status showed no local skill edits, but it is still the normal flag for a script-type change.

Quick check after upgrade:

```bash
.specify/scripts/bash/check-prerequisites.sh --json --paths-only
```

You should get JSON with `FEATURE_DIR` / `FEATURE_SPEC`.

## New projects

Pick the runtime at init:

```bash
specify init --here --force --integration cursor-agent --script sh
```

(or `--script py` if you prefer Python helpers)

## Alternative: keep PowerShell

If you want to stay on `ps`:

```bash
brew install powershell   # provides `pwsh`
```
